summary: Returns the value as a numeric value, or throws.
description: A finite number, or a string that converts to one. `NaN`, the infinities and the empty string are excluded, which is what separates this from a bare `Number(value)`.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a numeric value.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not convertible to a number.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireNumberLike(1); // => 1
requireNumberLike("1.5"); // => "1.5"
requireNumberLike(NaN); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNumberLike(Infinity); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
